title: Misleading costs
text: Only option to upgrade is 29:99 or 4:99 per month.  Then why does the App Store have a long list of options?

title: Please stop asking me to review this app
text: Seriously stop. I don’t know how many times I have to write this.

title: Massive price increase
text: Used to love this app.  Used it all the time, but just recently received my renewal notice and they are raising the price from $9.99 a month to $14.99 a month…. That is a 50% increase.  They claim it is to support new features but this app has been pretty steady for the past few years.  They are not really adding any massive new features to justify a 50% increase in membership fees…

title: Stop asking me to submit a review
text: Stop asking for reviews

title: Misleading
text: This app makes you pay for something that you can do for free.

title: Not updated
text: I used to love this app as an easy way to add custom interval plans. However, the app is glitchy now and you can’t save the names of any new plans making it useless to me. I hope they fix it

title: Mileage is off on my iPhone
text: The app serves a basic purpose but the mileage seems to be off. I’ve run with a partner using the same app and on a 7 mile run, we are of each other by a mile.

title: Adds
text: I couldn’t start my workout because of the annoying advertising. I will delete this app and walk without it!!!🙁

title: Subscription version now has ads
text: I have had a paid subscription for this app for years and have loved it. My subscription renewed at the end of August and now I get ads! I thought the paid subscription did away with the ads?  How do I get an ad-free subscription? I deleted the app and reloaded it but still have the ads. Very frustrating.

title: Better than Strava!
text: The cost is $9.99/year vs overly greedy Strava’s $80.00/year. I’e been using Runmeter for 10 years and it’s better and more consistent than Strava… and the free option is all you’ll ever need.

title: Won’t record to Strava.
text: The token won’t refresh.

title: Confusing interface, keep it simple!
text: I appreciate the attempt to pack millions of features into an app, but it has to be the most confusing user interface I’ve ever seen in an app. The free version doesn’t let you do much at all, but all the paid features are there anyways waiting to let you click on a nag screen. If I’m frustrated enough to throw the phone at passing road signs while testing  the free version, I’m sure as heck not going to dive deeper and pay for a premium version. Sorry, I’m deleting it and moving to something else.

title: GPS does work consistent
text: Had this app for years and it worked fine. Recently got back into running after a long break. It only tracks my run time- no other run data. That’s whole point of this this app. Phone GPS works just fine w other apps, but this one says poor GPS connection

title: Runner enthusiast
text: Terrible interface. For example, the Start button is designed narrowly such that when you have your phone on an armband and you’re outside in the sun, it’s very hard to see and tap on the Start button. What a stupid design - the other running apps have their Start button much larger. Also, the menus and functions are not very intuitive, the overall user experience is not good.

title: So Consistently Inaccurate
text:
Only works well when running in a straight line, in a wide open area, on flat ground.

During a recent 50k, the app was reporting 8 miles when the actual distance was 6.3 miles.  By the end, the app was reporting 39.38 miles on a 31.4 mile course. 

During a recent 50 miler, the app was reporting 52.57 miles.  During another recent 50k, it was reporting 37.08 miles, and one more was 32..82.

When the mileage is off so drastically, every other measurement is then off as well and is meaningless.  

App is set up according to the instructions on the site, re: bluetooth, wi-fi, etc., and iOS and app are updated.  

Hearing pace/distance/time announcements during races/runs used to be beneficial.  Now the only thing this app is good for is announcing the time.

title: Incredibly annoying ads!
text: The free version constantly overwhelms you with annoying and startlingly loud adds. Not only that but they make it really hard to close and find the x for closing.

title: “0.00 miles” - awesome, thanks for nothing
text: This app tracks my time but not my distance. Currently looking for a better app as this has happened more often than it actually tracks my distance.

title: The GPS is not precise.
text: The GPS is not precise. Done multiple activities in the same route cycling or running and distance is way to many miles when I run o to little when ride the bicycle an it show like I took a shortcut in the map.

title: GPS Topical mapping dosn’t
text: The geo earth mapping no longer works, despite taking your money the support provided is not helpful. I will be done with it when it expires

title: Audio split times
text: Would like split times told to me

title: Been using it for 7 years and still loving it.
text:
As a data junkie, Runmeter let’s me analyze individual runs as well as trends over time. 

It’s nice that the Watch app has been untethered from the iPhone but since I don’t have a Apple Watch with a cell connection, I always take my phone with me anyways so my wife can track where I am. 

Well worth the upgrade cost to the pro version.

title: Bad update
text: For some reason, after today’s update (8 sep 21) my Runmeter does not get the apple watch HR data. Rendering it useless. I’ve been using Runmeter for 8+ years and it’s been great, but if this doesn’t get resolved soon, I will have to switch workout apps. Please fix!

title: Use a different app 👎🏼
text: This was a great app years ago. Now almost every run it stops tracking my distance and pace. That should be the most reliable thing! Now the only part I can rely on is disappointment and ad’s after every input. Big fail 👋🏼

title: Annoying ads
text: Used to love Runmeter but now every time I access it I have to wait for some mindless ad to play through. Enough!

title: Can’t use Apple Watch stand alone
text: I should’ve read the reviews first. Unfortunately I don’t want to carry my phone around when I do workouts and prefer to use the Apple Watch. Will be deleting and cancelling my subscription.

title: Lots of potential
text:
First, they get 5 stars for support. I couldn’t get my Polar heart rate strap to work and I emailed them. Got a reply in less than 30 minutes, on a weekend, with a fix that worked. Pair it to the phone, not the watch. 

Unfortunately the heart rate does not update very often on the watch app. It seems to only work when the phone is unlocked. Beyond that, the app has tons of potential. Great stats for running and walking. However, the interface really needs some help. All the right info is there, but it’s not pleasant to look at or use. On the watch screens you have to scroll to see all the info. I also enjoyed the running plans, the interval training features, and the emailing of runs to let others know where I am. 

If the heart rate screen worked better on the watch I maybe would have paid the yearly fee. If it had that plus a better interface, it would be easy to pay for it. I’ll check back later to see how it develops.

title: Should you buy? It depends ...
text:
It is difficult to rate this app. I bought it due to the shameful lack of run apps that have a lap feature. In my excitement to purchase I neglected to see in the reviews - not in the description- that to use the Apple Watch you need to carry your phone. I bought the Apple Watch so I could run without a phone. So, if you are like me, this will be massively frustrating. (I’ve only used the app once because of this.) 

Lots of cool screens - if you can read them. The one time I was able to use the app I found it difficult to read all but one of the screens while in motion. No doubt they are slick to look at when you are sitting on your couch. Good luck trying to see data at a glance. 

This review does not cover any of the other notable features (e.g., plans) because I truly only wanted a GPS app with a lap feature I could use on my Apple Watch - again, without carrying my phone. I’ll keep looking for it.

title: Changed my review 👎🏽
text:
This used to be a 5 star review from me. My go to running app.  These guys just don't get it anymore. Apple Watch support but you still have to bring the phone?!? Talk about a disconnect with your user base. Not only that, these guys have about zero customer support. I'm so sad I've moved on from this once great app. Just take a look at more recent reviews than the overall rating. Much more disappointment than in the earlier years.

Update: Upped it to two stars ⭐️⭐️ The developer mentioned importing my info from the Apple Watch. Indeed you can, but you can only access that feature through a paywall, where other running apps just include this from your initial download. I did in fact pay to see if it works well and it does. I just wish I can use this app on my watch without my phone. If the developers can at least give us an update on the app and if they plan on working on a standalone app for the watch or even if it’s not in the cards.

title: Downgraded to 1 star
text:
I still love this app on the iPhone for the customizations but hate that it’s still not stand alone on the watch. It also, for whatever reason, has a problem with consistency on connectivity with the iPhone. I have my iPhone in my arm band on my left side and the watch on my right wrist and I get the no connectivity symbol often when running. Sometimes it just stops working completely with the app. Got to get with the program on stand alone with the watch. Until then I’m switching to Runkeeper who actually has a stand alone app for the watch.

Also, the notifications on the Apple Watch don’t work. It doesn’t even announce start or stop but the have them there available. Stupid. Cancelled my subscription.

title: Not a Standalone App
text:
Not one person in my parallel universe wants to lug an iPhone around with them on a 10-mile run, just to make this Runmeter App work with the Apple Watch. 

It’s gotta be a stand-alone app in order to bring me back. Otherwise, it’s seems like a decent app.

title: Was 5 now 2
text: I’ve been a premium customer for years and really love the app but they are tone deaf to AppleWatch stand alone functionality. Sure you can use Apple Workout App and then import it but why?  Get the stand alone watch functionality or become obsolete.

title: Keeps Crashing
text: Why does the app keep crashing in the middle of my runs? It’s updated, and I’ve started closing down all other windows to no avail. It is very frustrating trying to map and time a run when it crashes every half mile and stops. This used to be a wonderful way to track my runs-now it’s just frustrating. Yes I’ve emailed support.

title: No longer syncs with my Apple Watch
text: I used to love this app. But for several months I’ve had inconsistent syncing and now no syncing with my Apple Watch. I must move on...

title: Standalone watch app?
text: Is there a stand-alone apple watch app planned?

title: No standalone watch app
text:
This was the best for me past 5 years and well worth the premium subscription. I’ve stopped using it, unfortunately, and didn’t renew, due to the poor watch app that requires a phone to be carried along. 

5 star app if you run with phone, zero star app if you want to use just Apple watch.

title: Does not work with watch alone!
text: The whole reason i bought the watch was to leave my phone at home. The here app doesn’t support this and other apps do. So I like other features here better but I never again want to run with my phone on me. Improve the watch independence and I will use this app gladly again.

title: Run meter
text: Works great, keeps track of everything. It was connected to face book so when you are running and someone sees you on Facebook, they could make a comment and you could hear the comment while you were running and your friends could see where you were on the run. That doesn’t work anymore. Not sure how to get around it. Probably for safety reasons, but that goes both ways.

title: Mapping Issues
text: Has problems with coming back along the same path. Doesn’t accurately account for the distance because of this.

title: Requires You to Carry Your Phone
text: Despite cellular and other capabilities of the Apple Watch, this app requires you to have your phone with you.  I bought the app thinking it was standalone with the Watch...so beware before buying. Great app if you have your phone.

title: Watch App Stuck in Map Mode
text:
Excellent app usually.  I’ve used it for 6 years. 

Now the watch app is stuck in a map mode without stop start controls.  I’ve reinstalled to no effect.

title: Poor Apple Watch support
text: Great app for tracking progress, staying motivated and the training routines are a nice addition. Useless if you want to go running without your phone. The developer will not invest in standalone Apple Watch support. If you want to go running without your phone, find another app.

title: If you're looking for a watch app, look elsewhere
text:
Nowhere in the description does this app explain that it is so severely restricted that you can't test even the most basic functions. Until you purchase the full app, you get nag screens for nearly all of the icons you touch. If you attempt to open the app on your watch, it just tells you to go to your phone. With so many fitness apps in the market, I'm not willing to spend ten bucks to find out what the issues are for each. It's too bad, this looked promising.
Be honest in your description or give a real test capability!

title: Meh-support nonexistent
text:
Update:  I have tried twice to contact support and the emails have bounced back. Very frustrating. 

It has a ton of features that it’s impossible to know them all and a bit complicated to figure out. One of the biggest features that I liked no longer works. It used to post to Facebook when I was on a run and then read me all the likes and comments during the run. This helped get me through half marathon training and my first race in 2017. Now, I’m 2019, I’m training again and it no longer works. Might have to go find some other app.

title: App would be perfect if watchOS native
text: Great app marred by dependency on iPhone.  No valid reason at this point not to be standalone capable beyond lack of effort.

title: Music during running
text: All of a sudden I can’t listen to music while the app is running. I hope this is a bug and not on purpose

title: Poor Watch Support
text: They have chosen not to support stand alone support for the watch despite being available for a few years now.  I contacted their support and they said it was Apples fault and have no future timeline for adopting stand alone running with Apple Watch.  Strangely I have now been able to switch to several other third party apps that have been able to support this so their response to me seems interesting.

title: No Standalone Apple Watch Support
text:
It’s buried in the details, but it really should be more obvious because it makes no sense. 
It’s a beautiful app. Very full featured, but some some awful reason, it requires you to lug your phone with you.

title: Does not support stand alone watch use!!??
text: What a waste of a great app. I hate carrying my phone on the run. What is the purpose of having a watch app that requires you to carry the phone.

title: Outdated watch options
text: Have used all three apps for over 6 years so have enjoyed what they offer. I have never minded the yearly fee for the three apps. I figure a fee gets you continued development. That said hear we are with the Apple Watch 4 coming in a week and still no stand alone support for the watch. As phones have gotten bigger I have been wanting to leave it home. At this point if they do not announce stand alone support at least coming by December I will spend December testing other apps and move on for the first time in over 6 years.

title: Don’t waste your money
text: I got this in order to hear my stats. Unfortunately the accuracy is shocking. All the values, time, pace and distance were way off compared to my Garmin Fenix, e.g. the time was 25 min off, pace 7+min per mile off.

title: Use to ❤️ you!
text: It seems with the most recent update that the GPS is not working accurately anymore.

title: Inaccurate to a fault
text:
I don’t know why no one else has mentioned this yet, but the pace measurements are all over the map (literally and figuratively) in this app. I’ve been using this for a while and I’ve observed the following behaviors on a number of occasions:

1. It often stalls out and stops registering any change in time or distance
2. When it is working it often reports inaccurate information. For example, on a slight downgrade of a hill it reported that I was running a 5:30 pace, then on an equally slight upgrade it reported I was running a 10:00 pace. My pace was actually about the same on both hills. I’m not that fast, and I’m not that slow. At one point during my run it reported that my pace was 0:00 for about a quarter of a mile, at which point I turned it off and uninstalled it.

title: You need your phone with the Apple watch 🤦🏾‍♂️🤦🏾‍♂️
text: I bought this app, online it states using the Apple Watch app is a great, but I couldn’t find anywhere it states you need to lug the phone around too, 🤦🏾‍♂️🤦🏾‍♂️🤦🏾‍♂️

title: Useless Watch Support
text:
No stand alone watch support! You must have your phone with you to run this app. App works great on phone, useless watch integration.

Would like a refund since I paid for the upgrade to use with my series 3 cellular watch. As I run exclusively with only my watch, this app is useless for me.

title: Useless without Elite Upgrade
text: I've been a runmeter user since 2013 or earlier.  I upgraded to Elite in 2014 when it was a reasonable $ 4.99.  Then, in 2017 I STILL upgraded to Elite when the priced doubled to $9.99.  It's actually a great app, but without the Elite upgrade, it's pretty useless (to me, anyway).  Here's why.  I went for my first outside run in 2018 and didn't notice my Elite upgrade expired last week.  I spent about 20 minutes trying to figure out what was wrong with my heart rate chest strap.  It turns out you need ELITE to measure your heart rate.  You're kidding right..?  Nope.  How about just measure your steps..?  Still need Elite.  I didn't take the time to detail everything you lose without ELITE but for me, if a running app can't track my heart rate or at least steps, I'll just switch back to my fitness band or use a HR watch with my chest strap.

title: Mileage is off
text: I have used and loved this app for YEARS and recently, my mileage is off for every run. The shorter run, I don’t really notice. For my recent half, it was over by 1/2 mile. It then impacts your average pace that it’s telling you in your ear which for this same race, it was off by 30 seconds - which is a lot. Today I ran 6.5 miles and again, it was off. So disappointing Bc it’s been my go to running app for so long :(  I only gave it 3 stars bc of how long I’ve been using it.

title: It's ya boi
text: Trash

title: Problems constantly
text:
Runmeter is the most advanced running app.  But if you do anything with your phone or watch other than Runmeter you’ll have some problems.  If you like music on your runs, fahgetaboutit.  It just doesn’t work as intended nor ever consistently.

Simply put, I’ve been working with Runmeter for 6 years now.  Two years ago I gave up exclusive use and stopped depending on my running mates to forward me their workouts for correction.  It just never really worked.  

Since growing up and getting a Garmin device, I can at least use that and still use Runmeter to compare.  I like that Elite will log weather data.  But when your running app doesn’t do anything but the tertiary Wx logs, it isn’t really a “run meter” at all.

I’d say 4 years of hard work to make this thing work is enough.

If you just run and just use your phone to run Runmeter, *maybe* your mileage will vary.  Good luck.  You’ve been warned.

title: Intervals don’t work with Apple Watch independently
text: Nothing else to say. All I need is an app that has an interval timer and a run tracker! Thought this app was the answer! No Soup!!!!!

title: Used to love this, but no AW3 support.
text: I absolutely loved this app. Too many awesome, easy to use features to even list here. Been using it for years. But I bought an Apple Watch 3, and wanted to leave my phone at home. Too bad the Watch app only works if you have the phone on you! No thanks! So I will be abandoning this wonderful app after so many years. Please, please upgrade the app to use with the watch independently so I can come back!!!
